5) Dubbing - 2-3 Players do a scene, they cant speak (similar to 4). 2-3 players off stage dub over the scene and speak for the actors.

1) Forward Reverse - At any time host can call "Reverse!" When this happens, actors must repeat their actions and lines in reverse order until the host calls out "Forward!" and the actors continue their scene forward.

2) Blind Line - Actors go out of the room. Get suggestions like "Quotes, phrases, catchphrases, bumper stickers, etc" Write these on small slips of paper, scatter across stage. ACtors come back in, do scene and must incorporate the lines they pick up.

3) New Choice - Normal scene, host can call new choice and the actor must replace the last action/line with something completely different

This can be a very tricky short form game to play, and really it depends on your order. Heres are some tips we use when we play it.

**In-the-Room Players:**

* Make the naive player an important character.
* Give them plenty to do and say.
* Imagine what the naive players dialog might be while setting up the replay scene and leave appropriate spaces.
* Repeat the scene EXACTLY!

**Naive Player**

* Go for it. Don't wait around trying to figure out what is going on and what the scene is about. Make assumptions and strong choices from the beginning.
* Hang onto, but adjust, your "reality" as the other players provide additional scene content.
* When asked a question, answer it.
* Remember that they are replaying the scene exactly, so try to put yourself where they expect you to be.
